Definition: from G3584; to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature:--dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away).
BiblicalUsage: The seed on stony ground sprang up, but when the sun was up it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered away, and in the synagogue there was a man with a withered hand.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe withering is the parable's warning and the healing's proof: what has no root dries in the first sun, and the same withered hand that could not work is the one Jesus tells to stand forth and stretch out.
